newsitem.title: FINLAND: ASKO CEO SAYS LANOR SELLING TO MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ASKO CEO SAYS LANOR SELLING TO MARKET.

text.p: Holding company Lanor Oy has been selling stock in Finnish plastic pipes, furniture and white goods group Asko Oy, with the intent of winding itself up, Asko's chief executive Jarmo Rytilahti said on Wednesday.
"This spring and now ... the shares have been sold by Lanor," Rytilahti told Reuters by telephone, and said a statement would be issued soon.
More than 1.6 million shares in Asko changed hands mainly in big block deals brokered in-house at Merita Securities and Evli Securities at 92.00 markka and 92.50 markka per share on Wednesday.
Lanor was selling most of its Asko shares to the market "as part of a programme of measures aiming to wind up Lanor," Rytilahti said, but he did not specify how many shares were involved.
"They (the shares) have been sold to the market, they have been spread widely on the market," Rytilahti said.

Lanor would retain a stake of about one and a half percent in Asko, which would then be divided among Lanor's main owners, Asko, energy group Neste and insurer Sampo, in connection with the winding up of Lanor.
